Looking at these two statements:

(A) Defends monolithic services as "the best solution for everyone, because of the webscale"
(B) Defends microservices as "the best solution for everyone, because of the webscale"

Both use the word "Obviously" and reference "webscale," which are sarcastic markers. However, **(B) is the sarcastic one**.

Here's why: In tech culture, there has been a significant industry trend and hype around microservices, particularly in the 2010s and beyond. People have widely promoted microservices as solutions for nearly every problem, often citing "webscale" as justification—even when it's not appropriate for their use case. Statement (B) sarcastically mimics and mocks this very real tendency by exaggerating it to an absurd extreme ("best solution for everyone, because of the webscale").

Statement (A) is a defense of monolithic services against the hype, which is more of a counter-claim rather than sarcasm.

ANSWER: (B)
